newsitem.title: FRANCE: Peugeot's Calvet decides not to stand in election.
newsitem.headline: Peugeot's Calvet decides not to stand in election.

text.p: Jacques Calvet, chairman of French automobile giant Peugeot-Citroen, said on Sunday he would not stand in the forthcoming general election but would take part in the campaign to back President Jacques Chirac.
Calvet told Radio France Info he had changed his mind about standing for a seat at Levallois in the Paris suburbs because his candidacy would divide government supporters.
Another candidate has already been endorsed for the seat by the ruling centre-right coalition.
Calvet said he would nonetheless take part in the campaign "to bring (to the centre-right) the experience I have gained in international business competition."
He had been quoted on Saturday as saying that if he stood, it would be as a pro-government independent.
